CANONICAL_NAME.value: E 2.6 -- a superposition-based theorem prover for first-order logic with equality (Stephan Schulz)

VERSION.value: github.com/eprover/eprover master as of 2026-09-13 (commit in hashes; 3.x line)

value.lineage: Automated theorem proving by SATURATION: the resolution lineage (Robinson 1965) as refined into superposition/paramodulation with term orderings and a given-clause loop -- Otter (McCune 1988) -> E (Schulz 1998-) and Vampire, the engines that win CASC. Distinct execution model from every solver in the vault: it searches a space of DERIVED CLAUSES for the empty clause, proving a conjecture by refuting its negation. First theorem-proving fossil.

value.built_to: decide whether a first-order conjecture follows from axioms, by systematically deriving consequences until it finds a contradiction with the negated goal
value.pressure: the search space of derivable clauses is unbounded; term orderings, literal selection and the given-clause loop keep it tractable on real problems
value.success_means: a conjecture that is a theorem is proved (empty clause derived); a checkable proof object is emitted

value.pressure: unbounded search; combinatorial explosion of derived clauses
value.failure_condition: the prover runs forever or exhausts memory on a true theorem it cannot order well (incompleteness of the strategy, not of the calculus)

cut.note: saturation as the given-clause loop: pick one unprocessed clause by a heuristic, simplify it against the processed set (forward contraction), use it to simplify the processed set (backward), then generate every inference between it and the processed set and put the children back into the unprocessed set; the loop runs until the empty clause appears, the unprocessed set empties, or a limit trips; the heuristic is a round-robin over several weighted priority queues so that a cheap clause order (FIFO) and a small-clause order interleave

provenance.grade_basis: Techne FOSSIL_PACKET.json PROVENANCE_GRADE where issued, else the record's handoff string mapped (populated per R34; Harmonia may re-grade)

organs.human_name: ProcessClause (1560-1700): select from state->unprocessed; ForwardContractClause; ClauseIsSemFalse / empty clause; eliminate_backward_rewritten / subsumed / unit_simplified; insert into processed_pos_rules / pos_eqns / neg_units / non_units by shape; generate_new_clauses; Saturate (1738-1800): the while over TimeIsUp, set sizes, step / proc / unproc / total / generated / term-bank limits, then cleanup_unprocessed_clauses and the periodic SATCheck
organs.mechanism: each step removes the heuristically best clause from the unprocessed set, rewrites and simplifies it against the processed set (returning the empty clause if it collapses to a contradiction), removes processed clauses it now subsumes or rewrites, files it in one of four processed sub-sets by shape (oriented rewrite rule, unorientable equation, negative unit, non-unit) so later inferences can index by shape, and generates all inferences (superposition, paramodulation, resolution, factoring) between it and the processed set into the unprocessed set; the outer loop repeats while time and eight size/count limits allow, periodically grounding a sample of clauses for a SAT check
organs.output: the empty clause (proof) or a saturated set / limit
organs.state: processed (4 indexed sets), unprocessed (evaluated), the term bank, demodulator dates
assumptions: completeness of the calculus requires every inference between processed clauses to be performed eventually (the Otter loop's invariant); simplification is allowed because superposition with orderings is a saturation calculus (Bachmair & Ganzinger)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the loop is complete for first-order logic with equality and stops on many satisfiable sets; every CASC-winning prover has this loop at its centre
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the unprocessed set grows quadratically with the processed set (the limits exist because of it); the loop's power is entirely in which clause is chosen next
organs.human_prior: Otter (McCune 1988) given-clause algorithm; E's 'DISCOUNT loop' variant (Denzinger et al. 1997) where the processed set is kept fully interreduced
organs.source_boundary: ProcessClause and Saturate; MEDIUM because the inference and simplification bodies were not read

organs.human_name: HCBStandardClauseSelect (che_hcb.c 903-940): ClauseSetFindBest(set, current_eval); orphan removal; select_count vs select_switch[current_eval]; wrap at wfcb_no; DefaultWeightFunctions (che_proofcontrol.c 35-90): FIFOWeight, ClauseWeight, RefinedWeight, ConjectureRelativeSymbolWeight, OrientLMaxWeight ... combined as '5*X, 1*FIFO'
organs.mechanism: every unprocessed clause carries one evaluation per weight function (a heuristic control block holds a list of them); selection takes the best clause under the CURRENT function, then advances a counter; when the counter reaches that function's switch value the next function becomes current, wrapping around, so a specification like '5*symbol-weight, 1*FIFO' picks five clauses by weight for every one by age; clauses whose parents were deleted (orphans) are dropped on the way; weight functions range from clause size to conjecture-relative symbol weights that favour symbols occurring in the goal
assumptions: no single ordering is good for all problems: small clauses first is strong but starves old clauses (incomplete in practice), age first is fair but slow; interleaving fixed ratios gets both
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: fairness (every clause is eventually selected, via the FIFO share) with the strength of size-based orders
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the ratios are tuned per problem class (the auto mode, che_new_autoschedule.c, chooses them from clause-set features: unread)
organs.human_prior: Schulz 2002 'E -- a brainiac theorem prover'; the pick-given ratio of Otter
organs.source_boundary: the HCB selection functions and the weight-function registry

rejected_cuts.candidate: the inference rules and their indexing (superposition / paramodulation / equality resolution and factoring, CLAUSES/ and CONTROL/cco_*), term orderings (ORDERINGS/: KBO, LPO), the shared term bank and rewriting (TERMS/), literal selection strategies (che_litselection.c), clause-set features and the auto schedule (che_new_autoschedule.c), the PicoSAT-based SAT check, proof object extraction (PCL2/), the TPTP/CNF front end, the learning modules (LEARN/)
rejected_cuts.note: orderings + superposition are the calculus (Bachmair & Ganzinger 1994) and deserve a DEEP pass of their own; the term bank (perfect sharing) is a representation mechanism worth a cut

rejected_cuts.evidence: the loop, the selection heuristic, the calculus, the orderings and the indexing are separable and separately switchable by options

pressures.source_evidence: cco_proofproc.c Saturate / ProcessClause; che_hcb.c; che_proofcontrol.c weight-function defaults
pressures.condition: an organism derives consequences from a clause set; the set of derivable clauses is infinite; a proof exists among them; the score is proofs found within a time and memory budget on a problem library; the organism must also terminate on some satisfiable sets
pressures.failure_condition: starvation (a needed old clause never selected) or drowning (the useful clause buried under quadratic generation)
pressures.world_punishes: pure FIFO (slow) and pure smallest-first (unfair); no simplification (drowning)
pressures.world_rewards: interleaved queues, interreduction of the processed set, conjecture-directed weights
pressures.observable_consequence: problems solved within the budget on a TPTP slice with the selection heuristic set to FIFO only, weight only, and the default mix; and with backward simplification disabled
pressures.vacuity_condition: propositional or Horn problems solvable by unit propagation
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: a proof oracle (the world withholds it)
pressures.cheat_control: an organism given the proof's clauses as a watchlist (E has one: PreferWatchlist) must solve every problem quickly; FIFO-only must time out where the mix succeeds; the mix without simplification must exhaust memory on equational problems: the world must show all three
pressures.purpose_separated_from_pressure: PURPOSE: first-order theorem proving with equality (Schulz 1998-)
